chunks: ʿAlī, from al-Naḍr ibn Ṣabbāḥ al-Bajalī, from Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf al-Shāshī, who said:

A fistula appeared on my buttock, so I showed it to the physicians and spent wealth on it, but they said, “We do not know any cure for it.” So I wrote a note asking for du'a, and he (عليه السلام) wrote back to me: “May Allah clothe you in well-being and make you with us in this world and the Hereafter.”

He said: Not even a Friday passed over me before I was cured, and it became like my palm. Then I called a physician from among our companions and showed it to him, and he said, “We had not known any cure for this.”

key_terms.الدُّعَاءَ: supplication requested from the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.الْآخِرَةِ: the Hereafter, the life to come
key_terms.الْعَافِيَةَ: well-being, health, and safety from harm
key_terms.نَاصُورٌ: a fistula or severe boil-like lesion

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe healing through the du'a of the Imam عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a man’s illness for which physicians could find no treatment, after which he sought the du'a of the Imam عليه السلام. By the Imam’s written supplication, he was cured swiftly, and the report also expresses the hope of being with the Imam in this world and the Hereafter.
